title: Midweek handshake + runbook notes — Private Deployments (VPC/on-prem) — 2027-02-17
body:
Purpose: midweek sync + rapid postmortem of late-night handshake failure; capture temporary mitigations and runbook deltas to ship before next wave.

Attendees: Marisol (owner), Ethan (networks), Priya (field ops), Jordan (installer), Sam (SRE - async), Anna (customer success - Atlas Health).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Night of 2027-02-16 a Seedbox.ai on-prem deploy failed handshake during the final certificate exchange step. Root cause: asymmetric path MTU + kube-proxy conntrack TTL + aggressive firewall session timeout.
- Customer impact: control-plane stuck in 'joining' for ~2.5 hours, automated rollback triggered then succeeded; customer app degraded during window.
- Immediate mitigation applied: applied MTU clamp and bumped conntrack TTL to 600s; added preflight MTU probe to customer installer (hotfix v0.12.1).
- Follow-ups: add MTU probe to installer CI, add firewall session guidance to runbook, write automatic fallback to TCP keepalive in installer.

Standup logs (10:15 sync):
- Atlas Health (green): final network whitelist confirmation pending (security team wants list of egress FQDNs). Action: Priya to deliver FQDN list by 2027-02-19 EOD.
- Seedbox.ai (incident): see above. Action owners: Jordan (installer hotfix + PR), Ethan (verify other customers on same ISP path), Marisol (customer comms + RCA doc).
- NordicBank (amber): NFS mount performance surprising under load. Preliminary looks: NFSv4 async writes + 10Gb link oversubscription on customer's SAN. Action: open ticket JIRA-DEPLOY-3499 (Jordan) and recommend temporary FS cache tuning.
- New lead: onboarding checklist for edge-VPC installs needs a new step for BGP flapping detection. Action: Ethan to prototype a lightweight BGP flapping probe by next sprint.

Incident postmortem notes (seedbox handshake):
- Timeline:
  - 02:12 UTC: Installer reports TLS handshake timeout (client side).
  - 02:15 UTC: Reattempts start (installer retries 3x).
  - 02:35 UTC: Control-plane reports stale peer entries; conntracking shows sessions dropped intermittently.
  - 04:45 UTC: Hotfix applied (MTU clamp & conntrack TTL bump); handshake completes; cluster joins.
- Why asymmetric PMTU matters: our current installer assumes path MTU >= 1500; many on-prem networks with MPLS/VXLAN reduce effective MTU. Large cert exchange packets were dropped and ICMP 'fragmentation needed' was filtered by intermediate firewall.
- Why conntrack TTL contributed: cloud-router closed idle conntrack entries after 60s. Installer kept ephemeral timers expecting longer sessions; rehandshake failed due to missing state.
- Temporary mitigation rationale: MTU clamp forces fragmentation avoidance and reduces packet size; TTL bump keeps session state alive during long multi-step handshakes.

Runbook deltas (actionable items to commit):
- Immediate (ship this sprint):
  1) Add preflight MTU probe to installer binary and UI (Jordan) — test cases: 1400/1440/1500. Deadline: 2027-02-22.
  2) Update installer to fallback to TCP keepalive and shorter packet sizes if MTU probe fails (Jordan + Ethan).
  3) Add a 'firewall session timeout' troubleshooting section with sample iptables/ASA rules and recommended conntrack TTL values (Priya).
  4) Publish KB to customers with known ISP path issues (Marisol + CS).
- Medium term (next quarter):
  1) Add automated MTU/conntrack checks to private-deploy e2e tests in CI (SRE) with synthetic slow-paths.
  2) Installer telemetry: surface handshake phase + packet-size histogram in console for 30 days retention (product + instrumentation).

Open questions / discussion points:
- Do we want installer default to aggressive MTU clamp (e.g., 1400) for all on-prem? Pros: reduces hits; cons: might reduce throughput unnecessarily. Decision needed: engineering owners to propose a safe default.
- How many customers are on ISPs known to filter ICMP 'fragmentation needed'? Ethan to run a quick scan against customer IPs (low risk) and report by Fri.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Jordan: PR for installer hotfix and MTU probe (branch: installer/mtu-probe) — ETA 2027-02-22. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-runbook/pull/185 (draft).
- Ethan: run customer-path ICMP filter scan; list affected customers — ETA 2027-02-19.
- Priya: update runbook text and create KB draft — ETA 2027-02-21.
- Marisol: customer incident note + external RCA summary for Seedbox.ai — ETA 2027-02-20.
- Jordan & SRE: add MTU tests to CI (small synthetic harness) — ETA 2027-03-05.

Notes to self (choppy / todo):
- remember to add 'how to capture conntrack dump' snippet to runbook (conntrack -L > /tmp/ct).
- test MTU probe under IPv6 (didn't try last night).
- check whether dedicated Dedicated pool routing uses same conntrack TTL (likely variation per appliance).

Misc telemetry / anecdotal:
- Installer logs show a 2x spike in firewall error code 0x1b around 02:10 — might be false-positive from middlebox. Save logs in /shared/installs/seedbox/2027-02-16-02:10.tgz.
- Customer asked about auto-retry count tuning; current default = 3. They requested configurable retry limit exposed in customer YAML. Add to backlog (product).

Meeting cadence / handoffs:
- Next check-in: Friday 2027-02-19 10:00 PT (standup + hotfix review). Invite list: eng-private-deployments, SRE, Customer Success for affected accounts.
- On-call rotation: Ethan covers network on-call Thursday night; Jordan covers installer Friday morning.

Appendix: quick runbook snippets to paste in PR:
- Preflight MTU probe (bash): curl --interface eth0 --max-time 2 --resolve test.internal:443:<control-plane-ip> 'https://test.internal/_mtu_probe?size=1440' || echo 'probe fail'
- Conntrack dump guidance: sudo apt install conntrack && sudo conntrack -L | grep <tenant-ip>

End notes: this doc is intentionally sparse in places; will expand the RCA doc after Marisol finishes comms and Jordan lands the hotfix. Ping me in #private-deploys if anything needs to change before Friday.
